page: Microsoft Azure D16_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor based on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 8 physical cores, 16 vCPUs via hyperthreading, and a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Cache provisioning includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is set at 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, requiring network-attached storage for all operational and persistence requirements.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate solid mid-tier multi-threaded execution balanced by modest single-threaded throughput. The instance recorded 14885.14 in stress-ng multi-core testing, 7938.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and a PassMark CPU score of 15671.52, all aligning within the middle 50% percentile across evaluated systems. Single-core throughput is constrained, registering 1412.29 on stress-ng (bottom 25%) and a Geekbench single-core score of 1269.0. Memory throughput metrics show 82.97 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 45.16 GB/sec for uncached writes, complemented by a redis SET rate of 13.89 million operations per second.

Hardware instruction features include AVX, AVX-512 (F and VNNI), and AES, though advanced matrix acceleration extensions such as AMX are absent. While lightweight LLM tasks on a 135M model function adequately at 125.52 generation tokens per second, prompt processing on a 7B model drops to 22.86 tokens per second, reflecting the lower-tier classification. Given the absence of bundled local storage, storage performance and economics will directly depend on the attached remote disk configuration. Microsoft Azure D16_v4 serves as a balanced tier for web application servers, relational database engines, microservices clusters, and general-purpose enterprise backends.
description: Microsoft Azure D16_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL x86_64 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. It provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, 35 MB of L3 cache, and 64.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution. The virtual machine includes no local disk storage and lacks GPU acceleration, relying on remote persistent storage for disk I/O. Benchmarking reveals standard mid-range capabilities across multi-threaded applications, posting 7938.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 15671.52 in PassMark CPU tests, accompanied by modest single-thread capacity. Hardware vector support extends to AVX-512 and VNNI. The D16_v4 is primarily suited for mid-scale databases, microservices fleets, caching servers, and general-purpose enterprise application hosting.
